In February 1939 OLDAG went to the Continent where he stated he was in association with anti-Nazi refugees from Germany. He returned to this country from Geneva in September 1939. He was called up for military service in the Army (Pioneer Corps) on 17.7.41, and deserted from No. 12 Centre, Pioneer Corps on 27.3.43. He was not recovered till 27.11.44, when he was arrested by the civil power.

While a deserter OLDAG was in close touch with the anarchist publishers, the Freedom Press. In May 1943 they published his booklet "March to Death", which consisted of cartoons with captions of a grossly subversive and anti-war nature. The State, the Church and the war were all caricatured, and Churchill, Stalin and Hitler were all lumped together as being equally responsible for the sufferings of the world. In the spring of 1944 the Freedom Press published a further book of cartoons by him called, "The Life we Live, the Death we Die".

After his arrest in November 1944 he was tried and sentenced to 12 months imprisonment for a National Registration offence (being in possession of a National Registration Identity Card which was not his property). On release from Brixton in September 1945 he was tried by Court Martial for desertion and sentenced to 2 years detention, six months of which were remitted. This sentence has now been suspended.

There can be no doubt that OLDAG is still as convinced an anarchist as ever, but I feel that it would be valueless to place him under observation in the normal way and that we should gain nothing by asking for the usual type of report on him. Would you instead by kind enough to talk over the case with OLDAG's C.O., ask him to have an eye kept on the man, to inform you if anything unusual happens, and in any case to let you have his views of the case in three or four weeks time?
